title: Help Wanted: CEO, Preferably From Somewhere Else
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged Nvidia to recruit its next chief executive from outside the company, calling for a leadership reset after Jensen Huang’s departure.

Speaking on Fox News on Sunday, Bessent argued that the circumstances required substantial change. Reuters reported that Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent also demanded answers within 10 days about Nvidia’s compliance with export restrictions. Reuters cited a Financial Times report that Arm chief executive Rene Haas had been approached as a potential successor.

Nvidia confirmed on November 12 that Huang had resigned immediately as president, chief executive and director. The board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO, with Kress retaining her existing financial responsibilities during the search for a permanent replacement.

The company also named Harvey C. Jones as board chair. Nvidia said its search would consider candidates from both inside and outside the business, leaving its stated approach broader than Bessent’s recommendation.

The succession debate presents a difficult governance choice. An external appointment could signal independence and give a new leader room to examine management practices. An internal successor could offer familiarity with employees, customers and complex technology programmes. Neither route, by itself, would establish whether existing controls were adequate.

The distinction between allegations and established findings also matters. Questions about personal conduct, corporate oversight and export compliance require separate evidence; one does not automatically prove another.

For Nvidia’s board, the immediate task is to maintain operational stability while conducting a credible search. Its public statement expressed confidence in Kress and the leadership team, and said customer commitments and product plans should continue uninterrupted.

Ultimately, the appointment will be judged by the successor’s ability to lead the business, strengthen accountability and earn confidence through demonstrable performance over time.

Reuters — Bessent says Nvidia must “go outside the company” to find new CEO (November 15, 2026).
Nvidia — Official CEO transition announcement (November 12, 2026).
